issues.description: The problem statement requires a public constructor for Ride that takes all attributes in the order shown in the UML (name: String, then abbreviation: char). The solution's Ride class defines a constructor Ride(String name) that does not accept the abbreviation parameter and instead initializes abbreviation to a default value ('A'). This contradicts the specification and will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and how subclasses should call super(...).
issues.suggested_fix: Change Ride's constructor to match the UML and problem instructions: provide a public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) constructor that assigns both fields (this.name = name; this.abbreviation = abbreviation;). This makes the constructor signature explicit and aligns the implementation with the specification.
